stem:
Which of the following is correct for the given figure?

(The figure is a cut-away diagram of a chloroplast. Inside the oval organelle are several stacks of disc-shaped membranes. The label 'a' points to a single disc within a stack, 'b' points to a whole stack of discs, and 'c' points to a long flattened membrane connecting two stacks.)

options.label: A
options.text: The parts labelled 'a', 'b' and 'c' all possess photosynthetic pigments such as chlorophyll.

options.label: B
options.text: The part labelled 'a' is the site of dark reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: The part labelled 'c' is called granum.

options.label: D
options.text: The part labelled 'b' is called intergranal thylakoid.

stem:
Select the cell that contains starch. Name it.

(The figure is a microscope view of a group of plant cells. Each cell is packed with many oval grains that store starch, i.e. amyloplasts.)

Which characteristic of the nucleus in the given diagram is shown?

(The figure is a labelled diagram of a rod-shaped bacterial cell. Labels point to the pilus, capsule, cell wall, plasma membrane, nucleoid (DNA), cytoplasm, flagellum and ribosomes. The genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm as a coiled nucleoid with no surrounding membrane.)

Which cell organelle is shown in the given image?

(The figure is a cut-away diagram of an elongated, bean-shaped organelle with a folded inner membrane forming cristae. Labels point to DNA, ribosomes, matrix, outer membrane, inner membrane, F0–F1 complexes, cristae junction and intermembrane space.)

Mention the function of the cell organelle shown in the figure.

(The figure is a cut-away diagram of an elongated, bean-shaped organelle with a folded inner membrane forming cristae. Labels point to DNA, ribosomes, matrix, outer membrane and inner membrane — a mitochondrion.)

Study the given figure and answer:
1. Identify parts 1, 2 and 3.
2. An example where we see this structure is

(The figure is a simplified diagram of a cell. Part 1 points to the outer hairy covering, part 2 points to the inner boundary just inside it, and part 3 points to a single coiled thread of genetic material lying free in the centre. Small projections like pili/flagella surround the cell.)

options.label: A
options.text: 1 - cell wall, 2 - Nucleoid, 3 - Cell membrane; Bacterial cell

options.label: B
options.text: 1 - cell wall, 2 - mitochondria, 3 - Cell membrane; Plant cell

options.label: C
options.text: 1 - cell membrane, 2 - nucleus, 3 - Cell wall; Animal cell

options.label: D
options.text: 1 - cell wall, 2 - nucleus, 3 - Cell membrane; Plant cell

stem:
Identify the given cell organelle and mention its location.

(The figure is a diagram of a stack of curved, flattened membrane sacs. Labels point to the cisternae, the cis face, the lumen, the trans face, an incoming transport vesicle, a newly formed vesicle and an outgoing secretory vesicle.)

Identify the structure shown in the figure.

(The figure is a diagram of an oval organelle bounded by a double limiting membrane. Inside are several stacks of disc-shaped membranes labelled granum, flattened membranes labelled lamella, and a small osmophilic droplet, all in a ground matrix.)

subtopic: Plasma Membrane, Cell Wall and Transport
stem:
Study the given figure and answer:
1. Identify Cell A and B.
2. What happens when Cell A is dipped in a hypertonic solution and cell B is dipped in a hypotonic solution?

(The figure shows two groups of plant cells. Group A cells are plump and turgid, with cytoplasm pressed against the cell walls. Group B cells are shrunken, with the cytoplasm pulled away from the cell walls — plasmolysed.)

options.label: A
options.text: A - Turgid plant cell; B - plasmolysed plant cell. A will shrink up and B will swell and regain the size.

options.label: B
options.text: A - plasmolysed cell; B - turgid plant cell. A will swell up and B will shrink.

options.label: C
options.text: A - turgid cell; B - plasmolysed plant cell. A will swell up and B will shrink.

options.label: D
options.text: A - plasmolysed cell; B - turgid plant cell. A will shrink up and B will swell and regain the original shape.

stem:
Identify the black dots shown in the given figure and mention their function.

(The figure is a diagram of folded membrane sacs labelled Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum, with the membrane studded all over by tiny black dots.)
